https://www.politico.eu/article/us-russi.text: The global response to the Russia sanctions bill the U.S. Congress approved late Wednesday has been swift and defiant, with Moscow warning it would prolong its war on Ukraine, India vowing to protect its interests, and Beijing pushing back against what it called illegal “long-arm jurisdiction.” The bill, which U.S. President Donald Trump must still sign into law, would slap mandatory sanctions on Moscow’s leadership, energy sector, defense industry and “shadow fleet” seaborne delivery system for embargoed Russian fuel. It also empowers Trump to hit the five largest global purchasers of that fuel with 100% sanctions, a cudgel that has U.S. allies worried. China has bought 50% of Russian crude exports since 2022, India 37%, Turkey 5% — and the EU 5%. The bloc has also been the largest buyer of Russian LNG (49%) over that period, as well as the largest buyer of Russian pipeline gas (32%), according to data from the Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air non-profit. Advertisement Advertisement The bill “falls ​under the category of unfriendly actions, and of course the ​imposition of any additional sanctions by the U.S. would certainly complicate efforts to find a peace settlement in Ukraine,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov ​ told reporters Thursday . The Indian foreign ministry said New Delhi had previously “very clearly articulated” the potential impact of the measures on its relationship with Washington, and would “take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests.” Meanwhile, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Beijing’s trade relations were not “subject to interference or coercion from any third party.” As for the EU, critics of the sanctions bill argue it gives Trump too much leeway to issue waivers for major Russia supporters (e.g. China) with whom Washington is seeking wider trade deals, or conversely to pursue vendettas against U.S. allies who displease him, such as the EU , based on the oil and gas purchases of some member countries (e.g. Slovakia and Hungary). Trump has not said whether he will sign the Russia sanctions bill, although the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that he intends to do so, citing the White House. The European Commission has not publicly commented on the legislation.

Photograph: Charles-McClintock Wilson/NurPhoto/Shutterstock Virginia Elderly man allegedly beaten to death in Virginia Walmart by parents of employee Bert Atienza and teen worker reportedly exchanged words before parents showed up and allegedly attacked shopper Marina Dunbar Sat 19 Sep 2026 12.05 EDT Last modified on Sat 19 Sep 2026 12.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 77-year-old Walmart shopper died after he was allegedly attacked inside a Virginia store by the parents of a teenage employee he had confronted over a shopping cart incident involving his wife, according to US media reports. Bert Atienza died from blunt head trauma on 8 June, one day after the attack at the Walmart in Norfolk, Virginia, WTKR reported on Monday. The shocking incident was captured on surveillance video . Police responded to the store at about 3.20pm on 7 June after receiving a report of an assault. Girl orphaned by Super Bowl reporter’s drugging and a deadly Kansas crash is ‘extreme victim’, granddad says Read more Atienza’s wife, Josephine, was left on the floor holding her injured husband in her lap after the attack, according to video from the scene. “My husband was still able to speak, he said, ‘Help me get up,’ but I told him, ‘No, you’re bleeding. Your mouth is bleeding. Ambulance is coming,” Josephine said. “I look at him again. He has no more consciousness.” Atienza was found unresponsive and taken to a hospital, where he died from his injuries the following day. Medical officials ruled his death a homicide caused by blunt force trauma. The confrontation began while Atienza and his wife of 42 years were grocery-shopping after spending the morning at church. Josephine said a 17-year-old Walmart employee came quickly down the aisle where the couple was shopping and nearly struck her with a shopping cart. Atienza and the unidentified worker exchanged words before the employee allegedly threw a can toward the couple as they walked away, Josephine told WTKR. The teen then reportedly called her parents, Travis White and Erika Mitchell, who began looking for the couple inside the store minutes later. The store surveillance video shows what appears to be Atienza looking at items on a shelf when White and Mitchell approached and attacked him while their daughter watched. The elderly shopper was allegedly shoved from behind, grabbed and punched as people nearby walked away. He was then pushed into a shelving unit and fell to the floor, where one of the suspects allegedly kicked him. White, 44, and Mitchell, 42, were arrested days later and are being held without bond in the Norfolk jail. Their teenage daughter was also charged with assault and battery, aggravated malicious wounding, and conspiracy to commit a felony, according to WAVY . She is being held at the Norfolk juvenile detention center. Authorities have not released her name because she is a minor.
